plan.planning_summary: Refining route_01 based on iteration_06 score degradation (0.8497 → 0.6163). Four routes explore: (1) strict 550 nm quarter-wave initialization with expanded bounds per feedback directive, (2) increased layer count (28 layers) to expand design space, (3) dual-band weighted initialization balancing visible stopband and telecom passband, (4) chirped thickness profile to broaden visible reflectance. All routes maintain HfO2/SiO2 on fused silica, ≤30 layers, normal incidence. Parent_route_id fixed to route_01 per refinement_chain constraint.

routes.title: Strict 550 nm Quarter-Wave Initialization with Expanded Search
routes.scientific_hypothesis: Initializing all layer pairs at strict quarter-wave optical thickness centered at 550 nm (visible stopband center) with expanded thickness bounds and increased optimization evaluations will escape the local minimum observed in iteration_06 and recover or exceed the iteration_01 target score.
routes.design_principle: Quarter-wave Bragg stack centered at stopband center wavelength maximizes reflectance in the stopband; optimization refines thicknesses to maintain high visible reflectance while recovering telecom transmittance.
routes.proposed_topology: 20-layer alternating HfO2/SiO2 stack on fused silica substrate, air incidence. Layer 1 (adjacent to air): HfO2. Layer 20 (adjacent to substrate): SiO2. Exact count: 20 finite layers, 10 HfO2/SiO2 pairs.
soft_objectives: Maximize average transmittance in 1530-1565 nm band
Maximize average reflectance in 400-700 nm band
Maintain total thickness within manufacturable range
manufacturing_considerations: Individual layer thicknesses should remain above 30 nm for deposition control
HfO2/SiO2 material pair is industry-standard for space optics
theory_basis: Quarter-wave Bragg reflector theory: maximum stopband reflectance when optical thickness = λ_center/4 for each layer
Transfer-matrix method for coherent multilayer interference
expected_advantages: Strict 550 nm initialization places optimizer in visible stopband basin
Expanded bounds allow thickness exploration beyond iteration_06 local minimum
Multi-start strategy reduces risk of stagnation
known_risks: Quarter-wave at 550 nm may degrade telecom transmittance if not properly optimized
20 layers may be insufficient for simultaneous dual-band performance
Optimizer may still converge to similar local minimum despite re-initialization
routes.execution_request_english: Optimize a 20-layer planar dielectric stack on fused silica substrate with air incidence. Materials: alternate HfO2 and SiO2 starting with HfO2 at air interface. Initialize all odd layers (HfO2) at thickness = 550/(4*n_HfO2) nm and all even layers (SiO2) at thickness = 550/(4*n_SiO2) nm using material registry refractive indices at 550 nm. Optimization bounds: each layer thickness ±40% from initialization value. Use gradient_thickness optimizer with max_evaluations = 5000, multi_start_count = 20. Objective: maximize weighted sum of (average transmittance 1530-1565 nm) and (average reflectance 400-700 nm) with equal weights. Normal incidence, unpolarized light. Report best_target_score, valid_candidates, tightest_margin, and thicknesses_nm for all valid candidates. Canonical user controls: wavelength intervals 1530-1565 nm, 400-700 nm. soft objectives: High transmittance in 1530-1565 nm band; High reflectance in 400-700 nm band. behaviors to suppress or avoid: Low reflectance in 1530-1565 nm band; Low transmittance in 400-700 nm band. manufacturing constraints: Total layer count <= 30.
routes.revision_reason: Iteration_06 showed score degradation from 0.8497 to 0.6163, indicating optimizer stagnation in local minimum. Feedback directive specifies strict 550 nm quarter-wave initialization with expanded bounds and increased evaluations to escape current spectral basin.

routes.title: 28-Layer Stack with 550 nm Quarter-Wave Initialization
routes.scientific_hypothesis: Increasing layer count from 20 to 28 layers while maintaining 550 nm quarter-wave initialization will expand the design space sufficiently to achieve higher dual-band performance than the 20-layer baseline, as additional degrees of freedom allow better spectral shaping.
routes.design_principle: More layers provide additional interference degrees of freedom to simultaneously optimize visible stopband reflectance and telecom passband transmittance.
routes.proposed_topology: 28-layer alternating HfO2/SiO2 stack on fused silica substrate, air incidence. Layer 1 (adjacent to air): HfO2. Layer 28 (adjacent to substrate): SiO2. Exact count: 28 finite layers, 14 HfO2/SiO2 pairs.
soft_objectives: Maximize average transmittance in 1530-1565 nm band
Maximize average reflectance in 400-700 nm band
Minimize total optical thickness for mechanical stability
manufacturing_considerations: Deposition time increases with layer count
Stress accumulation may require compensation layers
theory_basis: Bragg reflector stopband width increases with refractive index contrast and layer count
Additional layers enable apodization and sideband suppression
expected_advantages: 8 additional layers provide more optimization freedom
Can achieve broader visible stopband and sharper telecom passband edge
May recover iteration_01 performance with better robustness
known_risks: Increased layer count may increase absorption losses
Optimization complexity increases with more variables
May exceed practical deposition tolerance budget

routes.title: Dual-Band Weighted Initialization at 550 nm and 1550 nm
routes.scientific_hypothesis: Initializing layer thicknesses with a weighted average between 550 nm (visible stopband) and 1550 nm (telecom passband) quarter-wave values will position the optimizer in a design basin that better balances both spectral requirements compared to 550 nm-only initialization.
routes.design_principle: Dual-band filter design requires compromise between stopband and passband center wavelengths; initialization reflecting both bands may find better trade-off solutions.
routes.proposed_topology: 20-layer alternating HfO2/SiO2 stack on fused silica substrate, air incidence. Layer 1 (adjacent to air): HfO2. Layer 20 (adjacent to substrate): SiO2. Exact count: 20 finite layers, 10 HfO2/SiO2 pairs.
soft_objectives: Maximize average transmittance in 1530-1565 nm band
Maximize average reflectance in 400-700 nm band
Balance spectral performance across both bands
manufacturing_considerations: Thickness initialization may produce non-standard values requiring calibration
theory_basis: Dual-band interference filter theory requires balancing multiple wavelength constraints
Quarter-wave condition at intermediate wavelength can provide compromise starting point
expected_advantages: Initialization closer to final dual-band optimum may reduce optimization iterations
May find solutions with better balance between visible reflectance and telecom transmittance
Tests whether single-band initialization biases optimizer toward one spectral region
known_risks: Weighted initialization may not correspond to any physical optimum
May degrade visible reflectance compared to 550 nm-only initialization
Optimization landscape may be more complex with dual-band starting point
routes.execution_request_english: Optimize a 20-layer planar dielectric stack on fused silica substrate with air incidence. Materials: alternate HfO2 and SiO2 starting with HfO2 at air interface. Initialize all layer thicknesses using weighted average: thickness = 0.7*(550/(4*n)) + 0.3*(1550/(4*n)) nm where n is material refractive index at respective wavelength from material registry. This places initialization closer to visible stopband while accounting for telecom passband. Optimization bounds: each layer thickness ±40% from initialization value. Use gradient_thickness optimizer with max_evaluations = 5000, multi_start_count = 20. Objective: maximize weighted sum of (average transmittance 1530-1565 nm) and (average reflectance 400-700 nm) with equal weights. Normal incidence, unpolarized light. Report best_target_score, valid_candidates, tightest_margin, and thicknesses_nm for all valid candidates. Canonical user controls: wavelength intervals 1530-1565 nm, 400-700 nm. soft objectives: High transmittance in 1530-1565 nm band; High reflectance in 400-700 nm band. behaviors to suppress or avoid: Low reflectance in 1530-1565 nm band; Low transmittance in 400-700 nm band. manufacturing constraints: Total layer count <= 30.
routes.revision_reason: Iteration_06 degradation suggests 550 nm-only initialization may bias optimizer toward visible band at expense of telecom. Dual-band weighted initialization tests whether balanced starting point improves overall score.

routes.title: Chirped Thickness Profile for Broadened Visible Stopband
routes.scientific_hypothesis: Using a chirped (gradient) quarter-wave thickness profile across the 20-layer stack, with layer pairs tuned to different center wavelengths spanning 400-700 nm, will broaden the visible reflectance stopband compared to uniform quarter-wave initialization while maintaining telecom transmittance.
routes.design_principle: Chirped Bragg reflectors broaden stopband by distributing quarter-wave conditions across multiple wavelengths; early layers target shorter wavelengths, later layers target longer wavelengths within visible band.
routes.proposed_topology: 20-layer alternating HfO2/SiO2 stack on fused silica substrate, air incidence. Layer 1 (adjacent to air): HfO2. Layer 20 (adjacent to substrate): SiO2. Exact count: 20 finite layers, 10 HfO2/SiO2 pairs with chirped thickness profile.
design_variables: All 20 layer thicknesses (nm) with chirped initialization
soft_objectives: Maximize average reflectance across full 400-700 nm band
Maximize average transmittance in 1530-1565 nm band
Maintain smooth thickness gradient for manufacturability
manufacturing_considerations: Chirped profile requires precise thickness control per layer
theory_basis: Chirped Bragg reflector theory: varying layer optical thickness broadens stopband
Gradient index structures can achieve broader spectral response than periodic structures
expected_advantages: Broader visible stopband coverage from 400-700 nm
May achieve higher average visible reflectance than uniform quarter-wave
Chirped profile may reduce telecom band ripple
known_risks: Chirped initialization may complicate optimization convergence
May reduce peak visible reflectance while broadening bandwidth
Telecom transmittance may suffer if chirping extends into near-IR
routes.execution_request_english: Optimize a 20-layer planar dielectric stack on fused silica substrate with air incidence. Materials: alternate HfO2 and SiO2 starting with HfO2 at air interface. Initialize layer pairs with chirped quarter-wave profile: pair 1 (layers 1-2) centered at 450 nm, pair 2 at 480 nm, pair 3 at 510 nm, pair 4 at 540 nm, pair 5 at 570 nm, pair 6 at 600 nm, pair 7 at 630 nm, pair 8 at 660 nm, pair 9 at 690 nm, pair 10 at 720 nm. Thickness for each layer = center_wavelength/(4*n) using material registry refractive indices. Optimization bounds: each layer thickness ±30% from initialization value. Use gradient_thickness optimizer with max_evaluations = 6000, multi_start_count = 20. Objective: maximize weighted sum of (average transmittance 1530-1565 nm) and (average reflectance 400-700 nm) with equal weights. Normal incidence, unpolarized light. Report best_target_score, valid_candidates, tightest_margin, and thicknesses_nm for all valid candidates. Canonical user controls: wavelength intervals 1530-1565 nm, 400-700 nm. soft objectives: High transmittance in 1530-1565 nm band; High reflectance in 400-700 nm band. behaviors to suppress or avoid: Low reflectance in 1530-1565 nm band; Low transmittance in 400-700 nm band. manufacturing constraints: Total layer count <= 30.
routes.revision_reason: Uniform quarter-wave at 550 nm may not optimally cover full 400-700 nm band. Chirped profile tests whether distributed center wavelengths improve average visible reflectance while iteration_06 showed uniform initialization limitations.

research_influence: Evidence s2-chunk:CorpusId:92993850:s2chunk:92993850:1765:3736:69b2ad685bc8c493 confirms telecom C-band (1550 nm) importance for satellite quantum communication, motivating high transmittance requirement in 1530-1565 nm band. No literature evidence found for specific dual-band filter design methods, so all routes are theory-based with quarter-wave Bragg reflector principles.

Prior iteration_01 achieved 0.8497 target score with 20-layer periodic stack; iteration_06 degraded to 0.6163 indicating optimization stagnation. All four routes address this through different initialization and topology strategies.
Feedback directive explicitly requires strict 550 nm quarter-wave initialization with expanded bounds, which route_01_refine_550nm_qw implements directly.
unresolved_decisions: Optimal layer count between 20 and 30 layers for this dual-band requirement remains unknown; route_01_refine_28layer tests intermediate value
Best initialization strategy (550 nm-only vs dual-band weighted vs chirped) unknown; three routes test different approaches
Whether visible band should be prioritized over telecom band in objective weighting remains open; all routes use equal weights pending evidence
plan.stop_if_all_routes_fail: Stop after the bounded route portfolio is exhausted or further search stagnates. Return every physically verified candidate and report soft objective trade-offs without a performance admission threshold.
